0-northborough-road-common-driveway.name: 0 Northborough Road common driveway special permit
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.description: Special permit application to allow 15 feet of frontage on an 8-acre parcel to divide the land into two residential building lots served by a common driveway.
0-northborough-road-common-driveway.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals approved a 15-foot frontage variance on September 16, 2026, allowing two proposed residential lots to access Northborough Road via an existing MWRA right-of-way, and accepted the withdrawal of the companion special permit application. Town counsel advised that the board had authority to grant frontage relief but could not override subdivision control or create lots. The project will still require subdivision approval from the Planning Board before the land can be divided.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 16 to grant the frontage variance and accepted the withdrawal of the special permit.
A speaker related to the applicant supported the variance, citing a past town approval allowing development access across water department property.

0-southville-road.name: 0 Southville Road apartment development
0-southville-road.description: Proposed construction of two apartment buildings and associated infrastructure at 0 Southville Road.
0-southville-road.status: The proposed construction of two apartment buildings at 0 Southville Road remains under review by the Conservation Commission. On October 8, 2026, the commission voted to continue the public hearing on the Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit application at the applicant's request. The applicant previously sought continuances to revise site plans in response to peer review feedback.

positions.detail: Has not taken a position on the application, voting 4-0 on October 8 to continue the hearing at the applicant's request.

0-valley-road-trail.name: 0 Valley Road footbridge and trail
0-valley-road-trail.description: Proposed construction of a wooden boardwalk and trail connection on Southborough Open Land Foundation land off Valley Road.
0-valley-road-trail.status: The Conservation Commission approved the Order of Conditions for the 0 Valley Road boardwalk and trail system in July 2026. While abutters raised objections over traffic, parking, trespassing, and wildlife disturbance, the commission found the Eagle Scout project complied with wetland protection standards. With the standard appeal period concluded, the project is permitted to move forward with construction.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0-1 on July 29, 2026, to issue an Order of Conditions permitting the boardwalk and trail project.
The Southborough Open Land Foundation supported the project for passive recreation, while Valley Road abutters opposed it citing on-street parking, traffic, trespassing, and environmental impacts.

1-overlook-drive-pool.name: 1 Overlook Drive swimming pool
1-overlook-drive-pool.description: Notice of Intent to construct an inground swimming pool, patio, and cabana within the wetland buffer zone at 1 Overlook Drive.
1-overlook-drive-pool.status: The Conservation Commission approved the project on October 8, 2026, closing the public hearing and issuing an order of conditions. Approval requires the perpetual maintenance of eight native mitigation shrubs and a pre-construction site inspection to review machinery access near the 20-foot buffer. With conditions set, work can proceed once the pre-construction access review is completed.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on October 8, 2026, to approve an order of conditions requiring native plantings and equipment access protections.

104-boston-road-water-appeal.name: 104 Boston Road water bill appeal
104-boston-road-water-appeal.description: Abatement appeal before the Water Commissioners regarding an underground leak and high water bill at 104 Boston Road.
104-boston-road-water-appeal.status: The water bill appeal has been resolved. Acting as the Water Commissioners, the Select Board voted on September 15, 2026, to grant a partial abatement, reducing the $2,872.03 bill caused by an underground leak down to $1,100. No further action on the matter is pending.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0-1 on Sep 15 to grant a partial abatement, setting the final bill at $1,100 to cover wholesale water costs and typical usage.
A resident urged granting full bill relief in light of the farm's historic presence in town and called for accelerated installation of smart meters.

14-newton-street.name: 14 Newton Street garage and ADU
14-newton-street.description: Notice of Intent to construct a detached garage with an accessory dwelling unit and replacement septic in the wetland buffer at 14 Newton Street.
14-newton-street.status: The proposed garage, accessory dwelling unit, and replacement septic system have received the necessary local regulatory approvals. The Conservation Commission approved an Order of Conditions in July 2026 following revisions to the roof-runoff infiltration plan. In August 2026, the Board of Health granted the required setback variances to accommodate expanded system flow despite concerns from the chair about expanding on a constrained lot.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0-1 on July 29, 2026, to issue an Order of Conditions after the applicant revised stormwater drywell plans.
Voted 2-1 on August 11, 2026, to approve septic setback variances, with the chair dissenting over permitting an expansion on a constrained site.

154-turnpike-road.name: 154 Turnpike Road site plan modification
154-turnpike-road.description: Major site plan approval modification and landscaping compliance for commercial development at 154 Turnpike Road.
154-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board is reviewing proposed site plan modifications to address site lighting and landscaping non-compliance at 154 Turnpike Road. The applicant has submitted updated fixtures and lighting dimmer plans to satisfy calculations, subject to board inspection. A draft decision is being prepared ahead of an extended statutory action deadline of October 23, 2026.

positions.detail: Reviewing lighting and landscaping remedies, with members conducting site inspections before reviewing a draft decision.

154-turnpike-road.next: Planning Board public hearing on October 19, 2026

170-woodland-road-coc.name: 170 Woodland Road Certificate of Compliance
170-woodland-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review for pool, patio, and drainage work within wetland resource areas at 170 Woodland Road.
170-woodland-road-coc.status: The Certificate of Compliance for residential work at 170 Woodland Road has been approved. The Conservation Commission voted 4-0 on June 4, 2026, to issue the certificate following confirmation that required mitigation plantings were healthy. The matter is now concluded.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on June 4, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance after the conservation agent confirmed required plantings were in good condition.

200-turnpike-road.name: 200 Turnpike Road site plan compliance
200-turnpike-road.description: Site plan compliance, occupancy permitting, and landscape performance bonding for a commercial facility at 200 Turnpike Road.
200-turnpike-road.status: The Planning Board has recommended approval of a full certificate of occupancy for 200 Turnpike Road after accepting a $30,000 surety agreement to cover outstanding landscaping and slope stabilization. The applicant was required to replace plantings and stabilize an eroded embankment slope by October 1, 2026. A one-year look-back inspection will occur in fall 2027 to confirm plant survival and slope stability before the bond is released.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22 to accept the $30,000 surety agreement and recommend a full certificate of occupancy.

200-turnpike-road.next: Follow-up inspection for plant survival and slope stability on October 1, 2027

2030-master-plan-update.name: 2030 Master Plan update
2030-master-plan-update.description: Strategy, funding, and consultant selection for updating Southborough's comprehensive Master Plan for 2030.
2030-master-plan-update.status: Preparations for Southborough's 2030 Master Plan update are in the early planning stages. The Master Plan Implementation Committee is recommending a hybrid approach pairing town volunteers with a professional consultant, funded through state grants or a Town Meeting warrant article. The Planning Board is weighing the framework and considering whether to establish a dedicated 2030 committee in 2027. The two boards are scheduled to meet jointly on October 19, 2026, to review consultant cost estimates and the overall strategy.

positions.detail: Recommends forming a dedicated Master Plan 2030 committee in 2027 and hiring a planning consultant under a hybrid model funded by grants or a Town Meeting article.
Has reviewed the hybrid consultant proposal and potential funding sources, deferring formal decisions until a joint meeting with the implementation committee.

2030-master-plan-update.next: Joint meeting of the Planning Board and Master Plan Implementation Committee on October 19, 2026.

21-coslin-drive-costco.name: 21 Coslin Drive Costco development
21-coslin-drive-costco.description: Site plan and special permit review for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco retail warehouse and 30-position gas station at 21 Coslin Drive.
21-coslin-drive-costco.status: The proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive is currently under major site plan and special permit review before the Planning Board. The Zoning Board of Appeals granted variances for retaining walls and taller light poles in July, but the broader site development remains pending. Key open issues include Route 9 traffic congestion, neighborhood cut-through traffic on Flagg Road, truck turnarounds at Route 85, and state environmental reviews. The Planning Board will resume its public hearing on October 19, 2026.

positions.detail: Currently reviewing the major site plan and special permit applications, with a town traffic peer review report pending.
Voted 4-0 on July 15 to approve variances for retaining walls up to 31 feet high and light poles up to 36.5 feet.
Residents raised concerns about Route 9 traffic congestion, cut-through traffic on Flagg and Southville roads, truck turning hazards at Route 85, and vehicle emissions.

21-coslin-drive-costco.next: Planning Board public hearing on October 19, 2026 at 7:00 PM.

21-highland-street-use.name: 21 Highland Street future use
21-highland-street-use.description: Planning for municipal department space allocation, community use, or potential sale of the town-owned building at 21 Highland Street.
21-highland-street-use.status: The Recreation Commission is planning to expand its use of 21 Highland Street for after-school programming and civic meetings as Youth and Family Services prepares to relocate. The department expects space to open up when Youth and Family Services completes its move to the Flagg School in late October. The building's long-term municipal future remains an open question following earlier Select Board discussions about a potential sale of the property.

positions.detail: Supports utilizing vacated office space at 21 Highland Street for recreation programs and shared civic meeting space.

22-newton-street-variance.name: 22 Newton Street garage variance
22-newton-street-variance.description: Variance petition under Section 174-8.3(D)(3)(b) to construct a detached two-car garage encroaching on side lot line setbacks at 22 Newton Street.
22-newton-street-variance.status: The variance application to construct a detached two-car garage at 22 Newton Street has been withdrawn. The Zoning Board of Appeals voted in June 2026 to grant the applicant's request to withdraw without prejudice following concerns regarding zero-foot side setbacks and blocked access for septic system maintenance. No further hearings are scheduled while the homeowner reconsiders design options.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 10, 2026, to allow the variance petition to be withdrawn without prejudice so the applicant can reconsider options.

22-turnpike-road.name: 22 Turnpike Road site plan modification
22-turnpike-road.description: Site plan modification to expand stormwater infiltration, permit existing patios and a shed, and address sports lighting at 22 Turnpike Road.
22-turnpike-road.status: The major site plan modification for the 22 Turnpike Road golf range is currently under review by the Planning Board while a draft decision is prepared. The Conservation Commission approved a negative determination of applicability for an equipment storage shed on the site in April. The Planning Board is scheduled to review the draft decision on October 19, 2026, ahead of its October 23 decision deadline.

positions.detail: Continued the hearing to October 19 while a draft decision is finalized, with a decision deadline extended to October 23.
Voted 5-0 on April 30 to approve a negative determination of applicability with standard conditions for a driving range storage shed outside the wetland buffer zone.

22-turnpike-road.next: Planning Board public hearing on October 19, 2026

229-parkerville-road-coc.name: 229 Parkerville Road Certificate of Compliance
229-parkerville-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and buffer zone encroachment resolution for a fenced garden at 229 Parkerville Road.
229-parkerville-road-coc.status: The Certificate of Compliance remains pending a final inspection following an agreement reached between the property owner and the Conservation Commission. Under the agreement, an existing split-rail fence may remain as the permanent boundary line, while gardening trellises extending into the 20-foot buffer zone must be removed to allow the area to revegetate. The conservation agent must conduct a follow-up site visit before the certificate is officially issued.

positions.detail: Agreed to allow the existing split-rail fence to remain and to issue the certificate once a site visit confirms trellises beyond the fence have been dismantled.

229-parkerville-road-coc.next: Conservation agent follow-up site visit in fall 2026.

250-turnpike-road.name: 250 Turnpike Road 40B development
250-turnpike-road.description: Comprehensive permit application under Chapter 40B for residential development at 250 Turnpike Road.
250-turnpike-road.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved the Chapter 40B comprehensive permit for the proposed 32-unit rental townhouse development in May 2026. The project remains before the Conservation Commission, which continued its Notice of Intent hearing on October 8 pending a peer review report from Lucas Environmental. Site wastewater plans also advanced in September when the Board of Health approved a septic variance for the property.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 6, 2026, to approve the comprehensive permit conditions and waivers for the 32-unit townhouse project.
Continued the Notice of Intent hearing on Oct 8, 2026, while awaiting a completed peer review from Lucas Environmental.
Voted 2-1 on Sep 15, 2026, to grant a 6-foot foundation setback variance for a septic pump chamber on the property.
Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to recommend a 90-day extension of the temporary certificate of occupancy for the site's storage facility.

34-turnpike-road-special-permit.name: 34 Turnpike Road special permit
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.description: Special permit review and zoning compliance for unpermitted construction and renovations exceeding approvals at 34 Turnpike Road.
34-turnpike-road-special-permit.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals conditionally approved 1.3 feet of side setback relief for unpermitted construction at 34 Turnpike Road. The approval requires the contractor to cut back an unauthorized foundation bump-out at grade and is conditioned on Board of Health confirmation that the septic capacity accommodates the home's bedroom count. An abutting property owner objected to the expansion, questioning the structure's overall size and septic adequacy.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 10, 2026, to approve the side setback relief subject to Board of Health certification of septic system capacity.
A representative for an abutting owner opposed the expansion, citing lot history and dwelling size and urging zoning relief be delayed pending Board of Health review.

355-turnpike-road-coc.name: 355 Turnpike Road Certificate of Compliance
355-turnpike-road-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review, unapproved paving, and stormwater maintenance for a commercial site at 355 Turnpike Road.
355-turnpike-road-coc.status: The request for a Certificate of Compliance at 355 Turnpike Road remains on hold before the Conservation Commission pending additional information. A site inspection identified unapproved asphalt paving, uncleaned catch basins with an oil sheen, and an uncleared stormwater outlet. The commission has tabled action until the applicant completes required cleanup, conducts stormwater maintenance, and provides engineering clarification.

positions.detail: Tabled the request pending required site cleanup, catch basin maintenance, and engineering clarification regarding unpermitted paving.

40-42-central-street.name: 40-42 Central Street site plan compliance
40-42-central-street.description: Resolution of site plan discrepancies, parking configurations, and occupancy permitting for 40-42 Central Street.
40-42-central-street.status: Site plan compliance and occupancy permitting for 40-42 Central Street remain unresolved while the applicant completes required accessible parking paving and inspections. The Planning Board previously recommended revoking the site's temporary certificate of occupancy and held an executive session regarding threatened litigation from the owner, while outstanding compliance matters also remain before the building commissioner. The Zoning Board of Appeals is set to resume its hearing on an appeal of the occupancy denial on October 21, 2026.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on May 11 to recommend revoking the temporary certificate of occupancy and met in executive session in June to discuss threatened litigation from the property owner.
Has continued the appeal of the building commissioner's occupancy denial to October 21 while accessible parking is paved, inspected, and compliance issues are addressed.

40-42-central-street.next: Zoning Board of Appeals continued public hearing on October 21, 2026.

55-plus-housing-bylaw.name: 55-plus housing zoning bylaw amendment
55-plus-housing-bylaw.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment to eliminate caps on age-restricted 55-plus developments and clarify affordability requirements.
55-plus-housing-bylaw.status: The Affordable Housing Trust is actively drafting revisions to the town's 55-plus housing zoning bylaw. The proposed amendment would eliminate the townwide cap on senior housing units while establishing a mandatory 12.5 percent affordability requirement and considering minimum lot size standards. An updated draft incorporating public feedback is being prepared for town counsel review ahead of submission to Annual Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Drafting bylaw revisions to remove senior housing unit caps and mandate 12.5 percent affordability.

6-walker-street-variance.name: 6 Walker Street garage setback variance
6-walker-street-variance.description: Petition to modify a 1965 variance condition and grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance to construct a garage addition at 6 Walker Street.
6-walker-street-variance.status: The Zoning Board of Appeals unanimously approved the application to modify a 1965 variance condition and grant a 6.5-foot side setback variance for 6 Walker Street. The board approved the relief based on lot shape and septic constraints that made alternative garage siting impractical. No further board reviews or municipal approvals are pending.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 15, 2026, to grant the side setback variance and modify the 1965 restriction, citing site constraints.
Abutters submitted letters of support for the application, and no opposition was voiced at the public hearing.

65c-school-street-coc.name: 65C School Street Certificate of Compliance
65c-school-street-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review following unpermitted brush clearing and wetland buffer zone remediation at 65C School Street.
65c-school-street-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a Certificate of Compliance for 65C School Street following completed remediation of the 20-foot wetland buffer zone. The approval came after the homeowner restored the disturbed area, planted native shrubs, and submitted an updated as-built plan demarcating the garden boundary. With the certificate issued, the review process is complete.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on July 29, 2026, to issue the Certificate of Compliance following buffer zone remediation.

66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.name: 66 Breakneck Hill Road septic variance
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.description: Septic system upgrade and wetland setback variance to support converting a commercial building to residential use at 66 Breakneck Hill Road.
66-breakneck-hill-road-variance.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved a septic variance for 66 Breakneck Hill Road on October 13 to accommodate converting a commercial building into a four-bedroom home. The variance permits an 85-foot wetland setback rather than the standard 100 feet, which improves upon the existing 79-foot setback and incorporates a nitrogen-reducing treatment unit. The project now awaits review and approval from the Conservation Commission.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 13 to approve the wetland setback variance contingent on Conservation Commission approval.

7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.name: 7 Turnpike Road bodywork compliance
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.description: Town bodywork permitting compliance and cease-and-desist enforcement for an unlicensed massage business operating at 7 Turnpike Road.
7-turnpike-road-bodywork-compliance.status: The Board of Health unanimously denied the establishment license application for Jojo Bodywork following ongoing noncompliance and operation under a cease-and-desist order. The board authorized staff and town counsel to draft and execute a formal written decision documenting the denial, citing missing practitioner credentials and unapproved operation. No further board proceedings on the matter are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on August 11, 2026, to deny the establishment license application due to missing practitioner certifications and operation during an active cease-and-desist order.

8-partridge-hill-road-variance.name: 8 Partridge Hill Road septic variance
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.description: Septic repair variance regarding groundwater separation and setback to the Sudbury Reservoir at 8 Partridge Hill Road.
8-partridge-hill-road-variance.status: The septic repair variance for 8 Partridge Hill Road has been approved. The Board of Health voted unanimously in August 2026 to grant relief for groundwater separation and reservoir setback to replace a failed 1975 system. The Department of Conservation and Recreation raised no objections to the plan, and no further board action is pending.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on August 11, 2026, to approve variances reducing groundwater separation to 2.5 feet and setback to the Sudbury Reservoir to approximately 230 feet.

911-field-bond-and-fees.name: 911 Field bond repayment and fees
911-field-bond-and-fees.description: Debt service repayment schedule and revolving fund athletic field user fees for the 911 Field turf complex.
911-field-bond-and-fees.status: The Recreation Commission is reviewing debt repayment schedules and user fees for the 911 Field turf complex after revolving fund revenues fell short of initial pre-COVID projections. Commissioners are weighing a repayment schedule of $30,000 to $45,000 annually through FY35 alongside a proposed $5-per-hour fee increase for sports leagues. Action remains pending finalized revenue models from the recreation director and finance director.

positions.detail: Deferred action in May 2026 pending refined revenue projections and fee models to address the remaining bond balance and a proposed $5-per-hour fee increase.

appointed-town-clerk.name: Appointed town clerk transition
appointed-town-clerk.description: Proposal to transition the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position, including interim clerk appointments.
appointed-town-clerk.status: The proposal to convert the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position goes before voters as Article 1 at Special Town Meeting, with an interim clerk currently serving through May 2027. Both the Select Board and the Advisory Committee unanimously support the transition to expand recruitment for an increasingly technical role. The primary concern raised involves the loss of direct voter control, prompting Advisory to recommend contractual termination-for-cause protections. If approved at Town Meeting, the change will require subsequent approval at the May 11, 2027 town election.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 to recommend approval of Article 1 to widen the hiring pool for a technical position, while recommending termination-for-cause contract clauses to address concerns over voter control.
Voted 5-0 to recommend approval of Article 1 after appointing an interim town clerk through May 2027.

appointed-town-clerk.next: Special Town Meeting vote on Article 1 on October 17, 2026.

board-of-health-body-art-regulations.name: Board of Health body art regulations
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.description: Revisions to municipal body art regulations regarding practitioner training, apprenticeships, and prohibited activities.
board-of-health-body-art-regulations.status: The Board of Health has approved updated municipal body art regulations, adopting them as enforceable local standards aligned with state model language. The revised rules restore training requirements for practitioners, establish standards for apprenticeships, and prohibit vaping in procedure areas. No further action on the revisions is pending.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on June 9, 2026, to approve the updated regulations with revisions including training mandates and a ban on vaping in procedure areas.

breakneck-hill-restoration.name: Breakneck Hill Conservation Land restoration
breakneck-hill-restoration.description: Planning and invasive species management for a comprehensive five-zone ecological restoration at Breakneck Hill Conservation Land.
breakneck-hill-restoration.status: Planning is underway for a comprehensive five-zone ecological restoration at Breakneck Hill Conservation Land to address invasive species, vehicle-related soil compaction, and damage to the beecology research meadow. The town recovered $47,000 from remediation contractors to help finance meadow repairs. The committee and town planner are currently drafting a formal scope of work to solicit bids for botanical surveys, site grading, and native replanting.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 4 to appoint a liaison for contractor invasive species work while drafting a broader restoration scope for bidding.

brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.name: Brox asphalt plant complaints
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.description: Intermunicipal response and MassDEP oversight regarding resident noise and odor complaints concerning the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough.
brox-asphalt-plant-complaints.status: Resident complaints regarding odor and early-morning noise from the Brox Industries asphalt plant in Marlborough remain under state oversight, as Town Counsel confirmed Southborough lacks regulatory jurisdiction over the facility. Although Brox installed a closed-loop exhaust mitigation system and MassDEP determined emissions meet federal standards with no known direct health threat, Southborough neighbors continue to report persistent odors. Southborough health officials are tracking local reports and urging residents to submit detailed real-time logs directly to MassDEP to assist state regulators.

positions.detail: A Stow Road resident reported persistent chemical odors and early-morning noise, requesting that Southborough and Marlborough jointly fund an independent air quality consultant to test for toxins.

cannabis-delivery-opt-out.name: Cannabis delivery opt-out waiver
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.description: Deliberation on whether Southborough should request a state waiver from the Cannabis Control Commission to prohibit adult-use cannabis home delivery.
cannabis-delivery-opt-out.status: Adult-use cannabis home delivery remains permitted in Southborough after the Select Board rejected a municipal opt-out waiver in August 2026. A motion to request the two-year waiver from the Cannabis Control Commission failed 1-4, allowing state-licensed retail deliveries to verified adults aged 21 and older. The issue is resolved, with no further municipal review or action planned.

positions.detail: Voted 1-4 on August 11 against seeking a two-year state opt-out waiver, leaving retail home delivery permitted in town.
Discussed the issue on July 7 with divergent views regarding youth access risks versus adult access and alcohol parity, declining to take a formal vote.
A resident supported opting out, citing skepticism over courier doorstep ID checks and arguing delivery offers no public benefit.

cemetery-expansion.name: Town cemetery expansion planning
cemetery-expansion.description: Site evaluation and capacity planning to identify and acquire land for a new municipal cemetery.
cemetery-expansion.status: Town cemetery expansion planning is currently in the site evaluation phase to address projected municipal cemetery capacity shortages by 2035 or 2036. The Cemetery Expansion Committee is finalizing an evaluation matrix to screen 58 candidate parcels of five or more acres, though town boards have not yet weighed in on specific sites. The committee is expected to present its final site recommendations before June.

classification-and-compensation-study.name: Municipal classification and compensation study
classification-and-compensation-study.description: A comprehensive classification and compensation study evaluating 48 non-union municipal employee positions.
classification-and-compensation-study.status: The municipal classification and compensation study is under review by consultant MGT, which is concluding data collection from surveyed peer communities. The Personnel Board has paused individual job reclassifications so all non-union positions can be evaluated collectively once the consultant reports. Final study recommendations will be presented to voters at the Annual Town Meeting in March 2027.

positions.detail: Voted to commission the study and approved the peer community list, holding off on individual reclassifications until consultant findings are complete.
A municipal employee objected to the board's decision to exclude Dover from the peer communities list, urging reliance on the consultant's independent process.

classification-and-compensation-study.next: Presentation of study recommendations at the Annual Town Meeting in March 2027

conservation-land-use-regulations.name: Conservation land use regulations
conservation-land-use-regulations.description: Adoption and amendment of town code regulations governing public use and activities on town-owned conservation land.
conservation-land-use-regulations.status: The Conservation Commission unanimously adopted regulations governing town-owned conservation land under Section 43-2 of the Town Code in April 2026. The approved rules incorporate recommendations from the Breakneck Hill Stewardship Committee. While the regulations are now in effect, the commission noted that potential future amendments could address issues such as exterior light trespass from abutting parcels.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on April 30, 2026, to adopt the land use regulations pursuant to Section 43-2 of the Town Code.

constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.name: Constitution Drive drainage and street acceptance
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.description: Sinkhole repair at 11 Constitution Drive and resolution of unrecorded municipal street and drainage easements.
constitution-drive-drainage-and-acceptan.status: The Select Board authorized the DPW to carry out an estimated $5,000 one-time repair of a recurring sinkhole at 11 Constitution Drive, contingent on a signed homeowner hold-harmless and right-of-entry agreement. Town staff and town counsel are investigating legal mechanisms to formally record the street and drainage easements, which were never deeded despite past Town Meeting approval. The driveway sinkhole sits over a 17.5-foot-deep town storm drainage pipe.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 2 to authorize the DPW sinkhole repair with a hold-harmless agreement and to pursue legal remedies for unrecorded easements.

costco-special-act-liquor-license.name: Costco special act liquor license
costco-special-act-liquor-license.description: Proposed special state legislation authorizing an additional off-premises liquor license in Southborough for Costco.
costco-special-act-liquor-license.status: Special state legislation authorizing an additional off-premises liquor license for Costco remains pending at the State House. The Select Board supports the bill and agreed to submit written testimony backing refined legislative language that gives the town two years to issue the license. No further town discussions or subsequent steps have been scheduled on the local record.

positions.detail: Agreed on June 16, 2026, to submit written testimony in support of the special legislation.

culvert-infrastructure-replacements.name: Culvert infrastructure replacements
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.description: Town-wide culvert replacements funded through a state grant to replace previously authorized borrowing.
culvert-infrastructure-replacements.status: Culvert infrastructure replacements are moving forward following Southborough's award of nearly $3.9 million from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program, which allows the town to avoid previously authorized borrowing. In August, the Select Board approved permanent drainage easements along Willow Street required for ongoing culvert work and state permitting. Town Meeting will eventually need to vote to rescind the original $3.9 million borrowing authorization.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on August 11, 2026, to accept three private drainage easements needed to advance the Willow Street culvert replacement.

downtown-wayfinding-plan.name: Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan
downtown-wayfinding-plan.description: A state grant-funded planning study to design and install directional, gateway, and informational signage across downtown Southborough.
downtown-wayfinding-plan.status: The draft Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan remains under review as officials evaluate sign styles and destination listings. The Historical Commission and Select Board have urged the inclusion of omitted historic landmarks like the Community House and Burnett Mansion, while cautioning against visual clutter and overly modern designs. Town administration plans to seek state One Stop grant funding to develop fabrication specifications and install the signs.

positions.detail: Raised concerns about sign clutter and suburban-style designs while urging the inclusion of omitted historic sites.
Reviewed the draft presentation and suggested simpler designs and additional historic locations before moving forward.

fay-school-25-middle-road.name: Fay School 25 Middle Road addition
fay-school-25-middle-road.description: Review of as-built plans, construction discrepancies, and landscape mitigation for an addition at Fay School's 25 Middle Road campus.
fay-school-25-middle-road.status: The Planning Board is reviewing Fay School's updated landscape mitigation and as-built documentation required to obtain a final certificate of occupancy for its 25 Middle Road addition. Open matters include verifying that proposed replacement plantings are native and certified free of neonicotinoid pesticides, addressing invasive species, and completing a pending engineering peer review. The board previously approved a temporary certificate of occupancy in August and will resume its review later this month.

positions.detail: Reviewing an updated native planting plan and awaiting completion of an engineering peer review before approving an enforceable agreement for a final certificate of occupancy.
A resident involved with local biodiversity urged the school to eliminate neonicotinoid-treated plants, avoid non-native species, and eradicate invasive porcelain berry.

fay-school-athletic-fields.name: Fay School athletic fields redevelopment
fay-school-athletic-fields.description: Notice of Intent and redevelopment to convert grass soccer fields to artificial turf and relocate a baseball field at Fay School's 0 Marlboro Junction property.
fay-school-athletic-fields.status: The proposed redevelopment of Fay School's athletic fields at 0 Marlborough Junction remains under review by the Conservation Commission. The commission has not yet evaluated the proposal on its merits, as previous hearings have been continued at the applicant's request or pending state DEP file numbers and peer review. On October 8, the commission voted to continue the public hearing on the Notice of Intent and stormwater management permit.

positions.detail: Has not taken a position on the application, voting 3-0 with one recusal on Oct 8 to continue the public hearing.

fayville-memorial-park-improvements.name: Fayville Memorial Park improvements
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.description: Planning, community outreach, and design improvements for Fayville Memorial Park, including splash pad features and parking capacity.
fayville-memorial-park-improvements.status: The park improvement project is under revision after the Recreation Commission withdrew its $1.5 million Community Preservation Act application from the fall warrant, deferring the request to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting. The Recreation Commission favors adding angled street parking along Central Street to preserve green space within the park, while the Select Board has requested further engineering and sight-line analysis before taking a position. Main open questions include resolving Article 97 open space restrictions, addressing neighborhood traffic safety concerns, and the outcome of an application for a federal Land and Water Conservation Fund grant.

positions.detail: Supports advancing park renovations with angled parking along Central Street (Option 2) and deferred its funding request to spring 2027 to address design and legal considerations.
Reviewed proposed parking layouts on Sep 2 without voting, requesting additional engineering details on sight lines and traffic buffers.
Residents voiced safety concerns about blind spots and vehicle speeds with angled parking on Central Street, while also raising questions about dog park regulations and oversight.

flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.name: Flagg Road and Route 9 hydrant relocation
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.description: Relocation of a frequently struck fire hydrant and removal of scenic road stone wall at Flagg Road and 361 Turnpike Road.
flagg-turnpike-hydrant-relocation.status: The Planning Board approved the Department of Public Works' request to remove approximately 10 feet of scenic road stone wall at Flagg Road and 361 Turnpike Road to relocate a frequently struck fire hydrant. The approval requires removed stones to remain on Flagg Road, with first priority given to adjacent wall reconstruction. With local regulatory approval granted, the town can proceed with setting the hydrant roughly 10 feet back into an acquired utility easement.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on May 11, 2026, to approve the scenic road wall removal with conditions governing the reuse of the stones.

fy27-road-paving-contracts.name: FY27 road paving and sidewalk contracts
fy27-road-paving-contracts.description: Procurement and contract awards for fiscal year 2027 DPW road paving and sidewalk maintenance.
fy27-road-paving-contracts.status: The contracts for fiscal year 2027 road paving and sidewalk maintenance have been awarded. The Select Board voted unanimously in September to approve the awards after bids came in roughly $400,000 below engineering estimates. The work will cover six roads, including interim maintenance on Cordaville Road and Cranberry Road.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to award the FY27 road paving and sidewalk maintenance contracts.

fy27-school-operating-budget.name: FY27 school operating budget
fy27-school-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, class size staffing, and reserve funding for the Southborough K-8 public schools for fiscal year 2027.
fy27-school-operating-budget.status: The Southborough School Committee voted in May 2026 to support a revised 3.99% operating budget increase for FY27 after adjusting offsets and limiting reserve fund drawdowns to avoid future deficits. In September 2026, the committee requested that the Select Board allocate an unanticipated $105,485 in Chapter 70 state aid into the town's Special Education Stabilization Fund to buffer against out-of-district costs. The proposed transfer of state aid currently awaits Select Board consideration.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on May 12, 2026, to endorse a 3.99% operating budget increase and later requested that surplus state education aid be placed in the special education stabilization fund.

fy28-operating-budget.name: FY28 operating budget
fy28-operating-budget.description: Operating budget planning, multi-year deficit forecasting, and consideration of a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override for fiscal year 2028.
fy28-operating-budget.status: Town officials are preparing the FY28 operating budget while facing a projected deficit exceeding $2 million, prompting consideration of a Proposition 2 1/2 operational override. Departments were instructed to submit dual budget scenarios—one level-service and one zero-growth—raising concerns among several departments about potential cuts to staff hours. The Library Trustees and Recreation Commission have approved their budget requests, while other boards are still finalizing submissions. The Select Board and Advisory Committee will begin joint budget reviews in early November.

positions.detail: Exploring a potential multi-year operational override to close an anticipated $2 million deficit and directed departments to submit dual-scenario budgets.
Counseled caution regarding multi-year overrides, recommending stricter fiscal discipline such as hiring freezes and evaluating pension borrowing options.
Voted 4-0 on Sep 8 to recommend a 5% total salary adjustment for FY28, pairing a 3% COLA with a 2% step increment.
Voted 6-0 on Oct 5 to approve its FY28 operating budget while balancing state materials expenditure compliance.
Voted unanimously on Oct 7 to approve its $4,250 operating budget request after clarifying trail mowing contracts.
Approved its small elected board budget but postponed a vote on its departmental operating budget options until Oct 20.
Voiced frustration over zero-increase guidelines that would force cuts to staff hours and delayed formal action to draft an explanatory memo.
Speakers suggested budget consolidation to improve efficiency but warned against changing traditional line-item presentations during an override year.

fy28-operating-budget.next: Board of Health vote on department budget on October 20, 2026.

glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.name: Glow SoBo holiday lighting
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.description: Funding and municipal installation of holiday lighting displays and kickoff event for the Tricentennial.
glow-sobo-holiday-lighting.status: The Glow SoBo holiday lighting display and kickoff event are approved to move forward for December. The Tricentennial Committee authorized a $10,456 contract for professional exterior lighting on municipal buildings and grounds, and the Library Board of Trustees approved decorating library property along with the installation of permanent outdoor outlets. Decisions on whether to open the library for after-hours indoor activities during the event remain deferred.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Aug 12 to approve a $10,456 professional lighting contract for town buildings and trees.
Voted unanimously on Sep 14 to approve exterior decorations and permanent electrical outlet installation on library grounds.

hopkinton-water-connection.name: Hopkinton MWRA water connection
hopkinton-water-connection.description: Proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water to the town of Hopkinton through Southborough's distribution system.
hopkinton-water-connection.status: The proposed intermunicipal agreement to convey MWRA water to Hopkinton is under review after negotiations resumed. Before contract terms can be finalized, Hopkinton must secure state approvals, Southborough must conduct an independent engineering review, and the Zoning Board of Appeals must review plans for a taller replacement water tank on Oak Hill Road. The Select Board plans to take up a vote to appoint special counsel to negotiate the agreement due to town counsel representing both municipalities.

housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.name: Housing and food health code enforcement policies
housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.description: Board of Health standardized enforcement procedures, violation correction timelines, and fee schedules for housing and food establishments.
housing-and-food-enforcement-policies.status: Draft enforcement policies establishing standardized violation procedures and fee schedules for housing and food establishments remain under review by the Board of Health. In August, the board tabled formal approval to allow staff to clarify how written compliance deadlines are determined based on violation severity. Revised policies were scheduled to return for board review in September.

positions.detail: Tabled formal approval in August to allow staff to clarify how compliance deadlines are determined based on violation severity.

kallander-field-repairs.name: Kallander Field turf repairs
kallander-field-repairs.description: Scoping, vendor pricing, and DPW coordination for repairing turf and playing surface conditions at Kallander Field.
kallander-field-repairs.status: Repairs to the turf at Kallander Field remain pending after the Recreation Commission received an estimate of $8,000 to $9,000 from the original installer, North Turf, with the Department of Public Works assisting with materials. The quote is significantly lower than earlier vendor estimates approaching $40,000 and falls within the commission's remaining capital balance of $13,000 to $14,000. A full presentation and decision were planned for June 2026, but the commission took no formal action and no further steps have been scheduled.

kratom-retail-ban.name: Statewide kratom ban and local enforcement
kratom-retail-ban.description: Local Board of Health enforcement and retail monitoring following the state's Schedule I temporary ban on kratom.
kratom-retail-ban.status: Following a temporary statewide order designating kratom as a Schedule I controlled substance effective August 2026, town health staff monitored local retailers to ensure products were removed from shelves. Staff informed the Board of Health in September that only one Southborough retailer carried kratom, and guidance was provided on returning or lawfully disposing of remaining inventory. No further local board action is currently required.

landfill-environmental-assessment.name: Southborough landfill environmental assessment
landfill-environmental-assessment.description: Environmental risk assessment, private well testing, and potential municipal water line extension regarding contamination from the Southborough landfill.
landfill-environmental-assessment.status: A proposal to extend municipal water service to two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill is heading to Special Town Meeting as Article 7. The $240,000 appropriation from water retained earnings would connect the residences to town water to eliminate contamination risks and avoid perpetual state-mandated well monitoring. Both the Select Board and the Advisory Committee recommend approval, with the town agreeing to cover service line installation from the street into the homes.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Oct 6 to recommend approval of Article 7 after confirming the town will cover the service lines from the street into the houses.
Voted 4-0-1 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 7 to extend municipal water service to the two homes near the landfill.

latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.name: Latisquama Road errant golf balls
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.description: Safety concerns and mitigation options regarding errant golf balls striking residential properties on Latisquama Road from the Southborough Golf Club.
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.status: The Golf Committee is reviewing mitigation options to address high volumes of errant golf balls striking residences and vehicles on Latisquama Road near the 7th hole. Members have discussed several course redesign ideas, including moving the tee box, reorienting the green, or shortening the hole to a par 3. The committee is keeping the issue on its agenda while awaiting input from the golf architect.

positions.detail: Seeking recommendations from the golf architect on potential redesign options for the 7th hole to mitigate neighborhood property damage.

library-book-drop-repair.name: Library book drop concrete repair
library-book-drop-repair.description: Repair and funding of damaged concrete beneath the Southborough Library book drop and clarification of municipal maintenance responsibilities.
library-book-drop-repair.status: The Library Board of Trustees approved funding the repair of the damaged concrete platform beneath the book drop using library State Aid funds, with work scheduled for early October. The board also moved to resolve recurring maintenance disputes by preparing a letter to town officials to clarify groundskeeping responsibilities between the library and the Department of Public Works. No subsequent actions or determinations on municipal maintenance boundaries have been reported.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously in May to fund the concrete repair through State Aid and to draft a letter seeking clarification on town maintenance responsibilities.

library-cpa-signage.name: Library CPA commemorative signage
library-cpa-signage.description: Design and wording of commemorative plaques crediting Community Preservation Act funding for Southborough Library restoration projects.
library-cpa-signage.status: Commemorative plaques crediting Community Preservation Act funding for library restoration projects have been approved and commissioned. Both the Library Board of Trustees and the Community Preservation Committee agreed on wording that thanks Southborough "residents" rather than taxpayers and features the town seal. Invoices have been submitted to the CPC for reimbursement to close out the grants.

positions.detail: Advocated for wording crediting "residents" and reported in August that the signs have been commissioned.
Voted 5-1 on July 21 to approve plaque language crediting the residents of Southborough with the town seal.

library-parking-lot-repaving.name: Library parking lot repaving
library-parking-lot-repaving.description: Capital planning, DPW coordination, and town warrant sponsorship for repaving the Southborough Library parking lot.
library-parking-lot-repaving.status: The library parking lot repaving project is currently on hold after being deferred from the FY28 capital budget cycle. Site engineering requirements to manage runoff and protect the water table significantly increased costs beyond what could be funded soon or covered by library state aid. The Library Board of Trustees plans to submit the project for town capital planning in two to three years.

positions.detail: Deferred submitting a capital funding request for two to three years after engineering requirements raised projected costs.

mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.name: McAuliffe Hearing Room audiovisual upgrades
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.description: Hardware, camera framing, and video conferencing upgrades for hybrid public meetings in the McAuliffe Hearing Room at the Town House.
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.status: Audiovisual upgrades in the McAuliffe Hearing Room have been installed and are currently undergoing fine-tuning. Recent adjustments include lowering front desk monitors to improve sightlines, while microphone calibration, camera framing, and in-room displays of remote attendee lists remain under refinement. Staff and technicians continue to work on resolving software and configuration issues as user feedback is monitored.

positions.detail: Supports the hybrid meeting upgrades and is monitoring user feedback as technicians address remaining microphone, display, and camera framing issues.

metrowest-recc-borrowing.name: MetroWest RECC borrowing authorization
metrowest-recc-borrowing.description: Short-term borrowing authorization of up to $12.5 million to bridge state grant funding for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center.
metrowest-recc-borrowing.status: The Select Board approved up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing authorization in May 2026 to serve as a bridge loan for MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center grant funding. The measure passed 4-1 following similar approvals in member towns Grafton and Westborough, allowing facility construction to continue without pauses between state disbursements. Opposition centered on Southborough taking on municipal borrowing risk for the regional district, alongside public concern over town liability for non-reimbursable lease expenses.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on May 19, 2026, to authorize the borrowing to maintain the regional dispatch construction schedule, over one member's dissent regarding regional district borrowing risk.
A resident expressed concern over town exposure to non-reimbursable lease, legal, and insurance costs, requesting financial agreements be posted to the town website.

municipal-grants-management-policy.name: Municipal Grants Management Policy
municipal-grants-management-policy.description: Town oversight and approval procedures governing municipal grant applications, match funding, and operational liabilities.

municipal-health-insurance-reform.name: Municipal employee health insurance reform
municipal-health-insurance-reform.description: Adoption of MGL Chapter 32B Sections 21-23 and collective bargaining with the Public Employee Committee to modify municipal health insurance plans.
municipal-health-insurance-reform.status: The town has accepted Massachusetts General Law Chapter 32B, Sections 21 through 23, authorizing expedited negotiations with the Public Employee Committee to modify municipal health insurance plan designs. The Select Board unanimously approved the statute in August to coordinate with Northborough and the regional school district on reducing premium costs. The parties are moving into formal collective negotiations ahead of planned implementation.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Aug 11 to accept MGL Chapter 32B Sections 21-23 to pursue plan design changes that lower premium costs.

municipal-health-insurance-reform.next: Implementation of proposed plan design changes on July 1, 2027.

national-grid-vegetation-plan.name: National Grid FY27 vegetation management plan
national-grid-vegetation-plan.description: Annual review and approval of National Grid's tree pruning and vegetation management plan along town distribution circuits.
national-grid-vegetation-plan.status: National Grid's fiscal year 2027 vegetation management plan is approved following a joint review by the Planning Board and the town tree warden. The plan encompasses routine distribution circuit pruning along Parmenter Road, Pine Hill Road, Nichols Street, and Clemmons Street, with contractor Northern Tree overseeing notifications and daily schedules. No full tree removals are included under the routine trimming plan, with any hazardous trees to be reviewed separately through joint hearings.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Aug 17, 2026, to approve the FY27 vegetation management plan.
Concurred on Aug 17, 2026, to approve the FY27 plan during the joint session.
A resident expressed concern about the aesthetic impact of roadside tree trimming and inquired about how utility specifications compare to town standards.

native-plant-landscape-regulations.name: Native plant landscape regulations
native-plant-landscape-regulations.description: Proposed Planning Board site plan rules and regulations mandating native plantings and invasive species management.
native-plant-landscape-regulations.status: The Planning Board unanimously adopted new Native Landscape Regulations for site plan review in May 2026. The regulations require all new vegetation in site plan review projects to consist of native species, prohibit systemic neonicotinoid pesticides, and restrict dyed mulches. More complex invasive species management requirements that were originally proposed alongside the native planting standards were deferred for separate study.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on May 11, 2026, to adopt the Native Landscape Regulations for site plan review as amended.

neary-school-building-project.name: Neary School building project
neary-school-building-project.description: Feasibility, design, and renovation or replacement planning for Neary Elementary School.
neary-school-building-project.status: The Elementary School Building Committee is evaluating renovation options for Neary Elementary School after voting to eliminate Option 4 and focus consultants on Options 1, 3, and a scoped $15 million baseline. Preliminary cost estimates range between $24.4 million and $38.5 million, significantly exceeding the earlier $15 million figure discussed at previous Town Meetings. Outstanding questions center on balancing code repairs with educational enhancements, preserving athletic fields and gym availability, and accounting for district office relocation costs. Project options are scheduled for presentation at Fall Town Meeting on October 17, 2026.

positions.detail: Voted on September 24 to eliminate Option 4 and directed consultants to focus on Options 1, 3, and a $15 million baseline scope.
Commenters raised concerns regarding parking, athletic field impacts, weekend gym access, and the potential costs of relocating district central offices.

neary-school-building-project.next: Elementary School Building Committee meeting on October 15, 2026.

neary-school-roof-replacement.name: Neary School roof replacement
neary-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed borrowing and debt exclusion to replace the failing roof and fund ADA upgrades at Neary Elementary School.
neary-school-roof-replacement.status: The Neary Elementary School roof replacement moved into construction over the summer of 2026 after competitive bids totaled approximately $2.8 million, well below the $4.5 million borrowing authorization approved by voters. Work was targeted to reach 85% to 90% completion before the start of school in late August. No subsequent updates or outstanding disputes have been brought before the School Committee this fall.

positions.detail: Supported proceeding with construction after combined bids came in approximately $1.7 million under the voter-approved $4.5 million budget.

opeb-funding-strategy.name: OPEB liability funding strategy
opeb-funding-strategy.description: Actuarial valuation, liability modeling, and long-term trust contribution strategy for the town's Other Post-Employment Benefits.
opeb-funding-strategy.status: Long-term funding strategy for the town's Other Post-Employment Benefits liability remains under review. The Select Board is examining Southborough's roughly 8 percent funded ratio and potential long-term approaches, including redirecting regional pension catch-up payments to OPEB once the retirement system reaches full funding around 2036. The town continues to contribute its baseline $250,000 annually while awaiting modeled scenario projections from actuaries.

positions.detail: Exploring contribution options and requested actuarial models targeting 80 to 100 percent funded status by various target years.

parkerville-road-utility-pole.name: Parkerville Road utility pole petition
parkerville-road-utility-pole.description: Petition by National Grid and Verizon to install an additional utility pole between poles 101 and 102 on Parkerville Road.
parkerville-road-utility-pole.status: The utility pole petition has been approved by both town boards. The Select Board approved the petition in June 2026 after National Grid agreed to shift the proposed pole roughly 1,000 feet away from direct abutters. The Conservation Commission also approved the roadside work and issued an Order of Conditions later that month.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 16, 2026, to approve the petition following an agreement to relocate the pole to an area without direct abutters.
Voted 5-0 on June 25, 2026, to issue a standard Order of Conditions after receiving a state DEP file number without substantive objections.

peninsula-trail-phase-2.name: Peninsula Trail Phase 2
peninsula-trail-phase-2.description: Scope, wetland crossing design, and construction funding for Phase 2 of the Peninsula Trail.
peninsula-trail-phase-2.status: Article 4 heads to Fall Special Town Meeting on October 17, requesting $217,318 in additional Community Preservation Act funds to construct a 65-foot pedestrian bridge along Route 30, bringing the total project cost to $428,550. Town boards are sharply split: the Trails Committee, Community Preservation Committee, Conservation Commission, and Recreation Commission support the appropriation, while the Select Board and Advisory Committee oppose it. The primary dispute centers on the project's roughly $5,000 per linear foot cost versus pedestrian safety hazards where the trail currently ends at the roadway.

positions.detail: Sponsors Article 4 to fund the bridge as an essential pedestrian safety solution connecting trail segments along Route 30.
Voted 3-2 on Oct 8 to advance Article 4 as printed without scaling back the $217,318 CPA request.
Voted 0-7 on Sep 16 against recommending Article 4, citing excessive costs of roughly $5,000 per linear foot.
Voted 1-4 on Sep 24 against supporting Article 4, questioning the project's cost amid broader town budget pressures.
Voted 5-0 on Jun 25 to send a letter of support for the revised bridge-only CPA application.
Voted 3-0 on Jun 30 to submit a letter of support for the Trails Committee's CPA funding request.

peninsula-trail-phase-2.next: Special Town Meeting vote on Article 4 on October 17, 2026.

personal-property-tax-exemption.name: Personal property tax exemption threshold
personal-property-tax-exemption.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to raise Southborough's personal property tax exemption threshold from $1,500 to $2,500.
personal-property-tax-exemption.status: Article 8 proposes increasing Southborough's personal property tax exemption threshold from $1,500 to $2,500 starting in fiscal year 2028, exempting 22 accounts to eliminate administrative costs that exceed tax collections. The measure is headed to Town Meeting with unanimous support from town boards. The Advisory Committee recently finalized its warrant report language detailing the minimal financial impact.

positions.detail: Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend approval, noting that administrative overhead exceeds the minimal revenue collected from 22 small accounts.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 8.

police-drone-program.name: Police Department drone program
police-drone-program.description: Proposed acquisition of a five-year police drone program package funded through unspent municipal personnel funds.
police-drone-program.status: The proposed five-year police drone program has been approved for funding and recommended for phased implementation. The Select Board voted narrowly in June to authorize the purchase using year-end department salary surplus, while the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee endorsed the safety priority but questioned the funding mechanism. In August, the Municipal Technology Committee unanimously recommended conditional deployment with operational privacy safeguards and formal follow-up reviews.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on August 27 to recommend conditional approval and phased deployment subject to operational safeguards and reviews at 90 days and 12 months.
Voted 3-2 on June 29 to authorize bottom-line budget surplus spending for the drone package, having initially excluded it earlier that month.
Voted 3-0 on June 24 to support the drone acquisition as an immediate safety priority, while deferring the funding mechanism to the Select Board.

presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.name: Presidential and Fisher Road waterline looping
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.description: MWRA loan funding and construction to connect dead-end water mains under CSX railroad tracks along Presidential Drive and Fisher Road.
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.status: The Select Board unanimously approved an application for a $1 million zero-interest loan from the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority to fund the project, which was previously authorized by Town Meeting. The project will connect dead-end water mains along Presidential Drive and Fisher Road under the CSX railroad tracks to improve water pressure and reduce bacterial buildup. The loan is expected to save the town more than $400,000 in interest costs compared to traditional borrowing.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Aug 11 to approve the $1 million zero-interest MWRA loan application for the project.

rescinding-unissued-borrowing.name: Rescission of unissued borrowing authorizations
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting warrant article to rescind unused borrowing authorizations for completed capital projects, including Breakneck Hill and the Neary School study.
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.status: Article 6 for Special Town Meeting proposes rescinding over $1.1 million in unissued borrowing authority for completed projects at Breakneck Hill and the Neary School study. The Select Board and Advisory Committee both support the article to clear town accounts and prevent unnecessary future debt. However, the Conservation Commission has requested preserving $100,000 of the Breakneck Hill authority to ensure sufficient funding for planned site restoration.

positions.detail: Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend approval of Article 6 to clear the books and prevent unneeded debt on completed projects.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 6.
Voted 4-1 on Sep 17 to ask the Select Board to reduce the rescinded borrowing capacity by $100,000 to retain flexibility for Breakneck Hill site restoration.

reserve-fund-transfer-policy.name: Reserve Fund transfer policy
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.description: Advisory Committee policy setting standard procedures, executive board oversight, and statutory criteria for departmental Reserve Fund transfer requests.
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.status: The Advisory Committee is in the process of updating its written policy and procedures governing departmental Reserve Fund transfer requests. The revised draft tightens guidelines to ensure requests cover extraordinary and unforeseen future expenses rather than retroactive reimbursements, while requiring executive board oversight and vetting by the town administrator. The committee is awaiting a clean working draft for final approval.

positions.detail: Working to finalize updated guidelines that tighten statutory criteria, require Town Administrator vetting, and prohibit retroactive reimbursements.

route-9-495-gateway-study.name: Route 9 and I-495 gateway corridor study
route-9-495-gateway-study.description: A joint $150,000 planning and infrastructure study with Westborough evaluating economic development, zoning, and infrastructure along the Route 9 and I-495 corridor.
route-9-495-gateway-study.status: Southborough is awaiting a decision on a joint $150,000 state Community One Stop for Growth grant application submitted with Westborough to study zoning, economic development, and wastewater along the Route 9 and I-495 corridor. The project has unanimous backing from town boards, with Southborough slated to provide a $7,500 local cash match if funds are awarded. The Planning Board conditioned its support on ensuring adjacent residential neighborhoods are safeguarded while focusing on commercial development opportunities. The Wastewater Study Committee is pausing further consultant work and meetings until the state announces grant awards.

positions.detail: Endorsed the joint grant application and decided on Sep 3, 2026, to hold off on retaining engineering consultants until award decisions are announced.
Voted 4-0 on May 21, 2026, to endorse an amended letter of support after adding neighborhood buffer protections and emphasizing commercial development.
Voted 5-0 on May 19, 2026, to approve an amended letter supporting the regional grant application.

route-9-495-gateway-study.next: State Community One Stop for Growth grant award announcement in October 2026

route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.name: Route 9 wastewater infrastructure plan
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.description: Planning, site evaluation, and District Improvement Financing for wastewater collection and treatment along the Route 9 corridor.
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.status: The Route 9 wastewater infrastructure plan is under active review and design development, with the Wastewater Study Committee deferring any warrant articles to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting. The committee and the Select Board support pursuing the project and exploring District Improvement Financing, though the committee determined it lacked sufficient cost and engineering details for the fall 2026 Special Town Meeting. Major open challenges include finding 15 to 20 acres for ground effluent leaching and resolving state environmental permitting issues such as Zone C water protection restrictions and interbasin transfer rules. Planning is currently focused on a modular, expandable collection and treatment layout along the south side of Route 9.

positions.detail: Focusing on a modular facility layout along Route 9 and targeting the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting to present financing and engineering plans.
Voted 4-1 in June 2026 to fund financial analysis for District Improvement Financing and voted 4-0-1 in April to extend the committee's charge through June 2027.

ruby-estates-subdivision.name: Ruby Estates subdivision
ruby-estates-subdivision.description: Six-lot residential subdivision along Lampson Drive off Mount Vickery Road.
ruby-estates-subdivision.status: The Planning Board has approved the surety agreement and released all six subdivision lots from their covenant following roadway binder and utility installation. The developer's bond covers remaining subdivision improvements. No outstanding issues or board reviews remain pending.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to accept the surety agreement and release all six lots from the subdivision covenant.

rural-cemetery-water-tower.name: Rural Cemetery stone water tower restoration
rural-cemetery-water-tower.description: Proposed structural evaluation, restoration, and Community Preservation Act funding for the historic stone water tower in Rural Cemetery.
rural-cemetery-water-tower.status: Funding and assessment plans for the Rural Cemetery stone water tower are deferred until the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting. The Historical Commission is preparing an application for Community Preservation Act funding to conduct an architectural and engineering assessment, having dropped earlier concepts to repurpose the tower interior as a columbarium. The proposal was postponed from the fall round to give the consultant time to document the structure and prepare bid specifications.

positions.detail: Agreed on Aug 3 to defer the funding application to the spring Annual Town Meeting round due to consultant preparation workloads.
Is advancing an application for Community Preservation Act funding to conduct an architectural and engineering restoration study.

sarsenstone-way-coc.name: Sarsenstone Way Certificate of Compliance
sarsenstone-way-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and archival records search for the 1970s Sarsenstone Way subdivision under DEP file 290-100.
sarsenstone-way-coc.status: The matter is resolved following the Conservation Commission's unanimous approval of a full Certificate of Compliance on August 27, 2026. The approval came after town staff located historic Department of Public Works as-built plans confirming road and drainage requirements were satisfied. The commission had previously granted a partial certificate in July for two specific parcels involved in probate proceedings.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on August 27, 2026, to approve the full Certificate of Compliance after records confirmed subdivision requirements were met.

scenic-road-tree-removals.name: DPW scenic road tree removals
scenic-road-tree-removals.description: Tree Warden and DPW hearings and approvals to trim or remove public shade trees along designated scenic roads.
scenic-road-tree-removals.status: Following a joint hearing with the Tree Warden, the Planning Board approved the removal of four trees and the trimming of one tree on scenic roads.

school-bus-transportation-operations.name: School bus transportation and technology
school-bus-transportation-operations.description: Bus operations, safety tracking technologies, and vendor performance oversight with contractor NRT.
school-bus-transportation-operations.status: Bus operations and driver staffing with contractor NRT have stabilized, with live security cameras and turn-by-turn GPS now operational. However, the rollout of student RFID tap cards has faced delays due to hardware and driver training issues, prompting district administration to pursue contractual penalty deductions. The School Committee accepted an update on the service in May 2026 without taking a formal position.

school-food-service-contract.name: School food service contract renewal
school-food-service-contract.description: Contract administration, financial performance, and annual renewals for district food services with Whitsons Culinary Group.
school-food-service-contract.status: The district's food services contract with Whitsons Culinary Group has been extended for the 2026–2027 school year following a unanimous School Committee vote. The renewal incorporated a 3.9% CPI fee increase and retained a guaranteed return provision after the program ran a net deficit through March 2026. District administration plans to evaluate Whitsons' performance later this fall to determine whether to continue into a third year or put the contract out to bid.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 13, 2026, to extend Whitsons' contract for the 2026–2027 school year with a 3.9% CPI adjustment.

school-food-service-contract.next: Administrative performance review in December 2026 to determine whether to rebid or continue the contract for year three.

senior-tax-work-off-policy.name: Senior Tax Work-Off policy and slot allocation
senior-tax-work-off-policy.description: Eligibility regulations and position allocations for Southborough's Senior Tax Work-Off property tax abatement program.
senior-tax-work-off-policy.status: The Senior Tax Work-Off Policy stands approved with an expanded allocation of 40 participant positions. The Select Board unanimously re-approved the policy in September 2026, adding CORI check requirements and exclusions for other employee benefits following earlier revisions that streamlined eligibility rules. No further board reviews or updates are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on September 2, 2026, to re-approve the amended policy requiring CORI checks and excluding other employee benefits.

southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.name: Southborough Golf Club Audubon management plan
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.description: Consultant RFP and environmental management plan to achieve Audubon International certification for the Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.status: The Golf Committee is moving forward with hiring consultant Conservation Works to complete an environmental management plan for Audubon International certification. After the sole $18,400 proposal exceeded available Community Preservation Act funding, the committee voted on October 13 to cover the $4,500 shortfall using its revolving fund and pay overdue membership dues. The committee plans to negotiate the final contract scope while working to demonstrate progress ahead of Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on October 13 to authorize up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to cover the consultant funding gap and pay past-due membership fees.
A resident inquired about past attempts at Audubon certification and funding set aside for golf course projects.

southborough-golf-club-irrigation.name: Southborough Golf Club irrigation replacement
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.description: Planning, value engineering, and Community Preservation Act funding for replacing the irrigation system at Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.status: A request for additional Community Preservation Act funding to complete a $1.087 million irrigation replacement at the Southborough Golf Club heads to Special Town Meeting on October 17, 2026. The Select Board, Community Preservation Committee, and Golf Committee support the article, which pairs roughly $433,500 in new CPA funds with $100,000 from the golf revolving fund and previous appropriations. The Advisory Committee unanimously opposes it, arguing that golf course capital projects should be self-funded through player fees rather than town CPA funds.

positions.detail: Supports the warrant article as drafted to complete the irrigation replacement without seeking floor amendments.
Voted 4-1 to recommend appropriating $433,546 in CPA funds subject to conservation and certification conditions.
Voted 5-0 on September 24 to recommend approval of Article 3.
Voted 0-7 against the article, contending the course should remain self-sustaining through player surcharges rather than CPA funds.
Reached consensus supporting the proposed design, including directional utility boring and a pump station under the conservation restriction.

sta-unit-c-contract.name: Southborough Teachers Association Unit C contract
sta-unit-c-contract.description: Three-year collective bargaining agreement between the Southborough School Committee and the Southborough Teachers Association covering Unit C support staff.
sta-unit-c-contract.status: The Southborough School Committee unanimously approved a three-year collective bargaining agreement with the Southborough Teachers Association for Unit C in June 2026.
