The contract covers administrative assistants and educational support professionals following what administration described as collaborative negotiations. The agreement was slated to be made public once ratified by both parties.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 18, 2026, to approve the three-year contract following collaborative negotiations.

stewardship-committee-structure.name: Stewardship Committee structure and merger proposal
stewardship-committee-structure.description: Deliberation over committee appointments and a proposal to merge the Stewardship Committee with the Open Space Preservation Commission.
stewardship-committee-structure.status: The Select Board resolved immediate membership questions on August 11, 2026, voting 4-1 to amend the Stewardship Committee charge to add an at-large seat and appointing Freddie Gillespie. Both the Stewardship Committee and the Conservation Commission oppose merging Stewardship with the Open Space Preservation Commission, arguing its land management role should remain distinct. While Select Board members have discussed conducting broader reviews of conservation and open space committee structures, no consolidation plan is currently scheduled for action.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 to convert the disputed seat into an at-large position and appointed Freddie Gillespie 5-0, while keeping broader reviews of committee consolidation open.
Opposes merging with the Open Space Preservation Commission, maintaining that it should remain an independent entity focused strictly on managing Breakneck Hill and the Town Forest.
Voted 5-0 on June 25, 2026, to send a letter opposing consolidation and urging the Select Board to preserve the Stewardship Committee's separate mission.
Commenters spoke in favor of reappointing Freddie Gillespie, emphasizing her extensive conservation record, volunteer commitment, and habitat management expertise.

stormwater-enterprise-fund.name: Stormwater enterprise fund
stormwater-enterprise-fund.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to establish a municipal enterprise fund for stormwater management accounting and future funding.
stormwater-enterprise-fund.status: A proposed warrant article to establish a municipal stormwater enterprise fund starting in fiscal year 2028 is awaiting Town Meeting consideration. Both the Advisory Committee and the Select Board have voted to recommend approval of Article 5. Officials have emphasized that the measure creates only an accounting framework, meaning any future fee structure or operating budget would require separate Town Meeting approval.

positions.detail: Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend approval, later adjusting report language to clarify that creating the fund does not implement any fees.
Voted 4-1 on Sep 15 to recommend approval after examining cost modeling that would eventually bill properties based on impervious surface area.

street-tree-planting-program.name: Street tree planting pilot study
street-tree-planting-program.description: A pilot study and planting program to evaluate street canopy cover and identify replacement tree planting locations.
street-tree-planting-program.status: The street tree planting pilot study has been approved and funded. The Planning Board unanimously authorized $5,500 from the tree fund for Davey Resource Group to assess canopy cover along 10 to 15 streets and locate approximately 25 replacement planting sites. A board member was designated as liaison to work with the tree warden on the project.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to approve the $5,500 pilot study proposal from Davey Resource Group.

town-budget-process-policy.name: Town budget process policy
town-budget-process-policy.description: Draft municipal policy formalizing timelines, board responsibilities, and procedures for constructing the annual town omnibus budget.
town-budget-process-policy.status: The draft town budget process policy is currently on hold following the Select Board's decision to table the measure on September 15. The primary dispute involves defining the division of responsibilities among the Select Board, Town Administrator, and Advisory Committee in developing the budget and preparing warrants. The Select Board is awaiting legal guidance from Town Counsel and clarification from the state Department of Revenue before taking further action.

positions.detail: Tabled the draft policy on Sep 15 to seek clarification from Town Counsel and state officials regarding statutory versus advisory committee roles.
Drafted revisions to protect its independent authority to evaluate, present, and defend the budget at Town Meeting, while expressing concern that the policy omits school spending.

town-common-fence-restoration.name: Town Common fence restoration
town-common-fence-restoration.description: Repair and restoration of the historic fence and railings at the Town Common funded by the Community Preservation Act.
town-common-fence-restoration.status: The Town Common fence and railing restoration is moving forward after the Select Board awarded the base contract to Kneeland Construction. Total base project costs, including engineering and construction oversight, are estimated at $82,000 to $83,000, within the project's $120,000 Community Preservation Act funding. The town plans to address a missing section lost during state highway construction separately through MassDOT or a future bid.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on June 2, 2026, to award the $70,500 base restoration contract to Kneeland Construction.

town-forest-footbridge.name: Town Forest Eagle Scout footbridge
town-forest-footbridge.description: Construction materials, permitting, and approvals for an Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest.
town-forest-footbridge.status: The Stewardship Committee has authorized the use of pre-cut pressure-treated lumber for the Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest. The approval followed a review of findings indicating that modern treated wood poses minimal risk to the surrounding wetland and vernal pool. No further committee reviews or subsequent steps are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 4 to approve using pre-cut pressure-treated wood, citing findings that modern treated lumber leaches minimal chemicals into wetlands.

town-governance-study.name: Town governance structure study
town-governance-study.description: A consultant-led study evaluating Southborough's municipal government structure, town manager authority, and committee organization.
town-governance-study.status: The town government structure study is currently underway, with consultant Capital Strategic Strategies presenting an initial overview to the Select Board in early October. The study is evaluating Southborough's governance model, town manager authority, charter versus bylaws, and the town's 68 committees. The 18-week project was commissioned to identify organizational efficiencies and reporting improvements.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on Aug 11 to award the $24,650 study contract, with one member dissenting over spending during impending budget deficits.

town-satisfaction-survey.name: 2026 Town Satisfaction Survey
town-satisfaction-survey.description: Design, public outreach, and execution of the townwide resident satisfaction survey conducted by the Municipal Technology Committee.
town-satisfaction-survey.status: The 2026 Southborough Satisfaction Survey is currently open to residents and running through November 30. The Municipal Technology Committee streamlined the questions and added sections on affordable housing and Council on Aging services to address drop-off rates seen in previous years. Following outreach at community events earlier in the month, the survey remains active online.

positions.detail: Organizing and conducting the 2026 survey, focusing on streamlined questions and expanded community outreach to boost response and completion rates.
Drafted and submitted recommendations on housing questions, clarifying terminology around development types and locations for inclusion in the survey.

town-website-redesign.name: Town website redesign
town-website-redesign.description: Redesign of the municipal website with vendor CivicPlus and consolidation of standalone departmental pages.
town-website-redesign.status: The municipal website redesign is currently in preparation, with implementation targeted for early 2027. Contract and module discussions with vendor CivicPlus are scheduled to begin around November. Committee discussions have also focused on the lack of dedicated town communications staff to oversee content and messaging, as well as plans to review web analytics ahead of the overhaul.
town-website-redesign.next: Contract and module discussions with CivicPlus are expected to begin in November 2026.

transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.name: Transfer station fees and regulations
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.description: Department of Public Works updates to transfer station sticker pricing, outside hauling costs, and operational rules for disposal.
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.status: The Select Board has approved updated transfer station rules and FY27 permit fees, and voted to remain in a 35-community municipal consortium to negotiate its next regional waste disposal contract. Under the revised regulations, the Department of Public Works clarified Swap Shop operations and excluded child car seats based on pediatric safety advice. The town retains the right to review individual contract terms as consortium negotiations proceed ahead of the current disposal agreement's December 2027 expiration.

positions.detail: Unanimously approved updated facility rules in August and voted in September to continue participating in the regional consortium for refuse disposal negotiations.

tricentennial-firefighters-muster.name: 2027 Tricentennial Firefighter's Muster
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.description: Organization of a regional firefighter's muster and antique hand tub demonstration at Woodward School in July 2027.
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.status: Planning for the July 17, 2027 antique firefighter's muster at Woodward School is underway under a $25,000 budget authorized by the Tricentennial Committee. Eight antique fire pumping apparatus teams have confirmed participation, with organizers expecting up to 20 teams alongside demonstrations by Southborough's restored historic hand tubs. Organizers are currently preparing site and parking layouts to submit to the committee next month.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on June 10, 2026, to approve an event budget not to exceed $25,000 and is overseeing ongoing event logistics.

tricentennial-firefighters-muster.next: Presentation of site and parking layouts at the Tricentennial Committee meeting in November 2026.

tricentennial-first-day.name: First Day 2027 celebration
tricentennial-first-day.description: Planning for Southborough's January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff celebration featuring family activities, a drone show, and a bonfire.
tricentennial-first-day.status: Planning is underway for the town's January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff celebration, with a contract executed for a 200-drone aerial light show launching from St. Mark's field. The Tricentennial Committee is currently adjusting logistical details for other activities, including considering tractor wagons instead of costly horse-drawn rides. Potential field damage and wiring concerns at Woodward School have also prompted committee members to reconsider the bonfire's timing and location. Committee leaders and staff will inspect prospective bonfire sites during an upcoming site walk.

positions.detail: Finalized the drone show contract and is actively organizing kickoff activities while resolving venue and cost logistics for the bonfire and hayrides.

tricentennial-first-day.next: Site walk to evaluate bonfire locations on October 18, 2026.

tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.name: 2027 Tricentennial Heritage Day Parade
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.description: Planning for an expanded Heritage Day Parade in October 2027 featuring marching units, community floats, and a historic cannon.
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.status: Planning for the 2027 Tricentennial Heritage Day Parade remains underway as the Tricentennial Committee evaluates route options and logistics. The committee is focused on addressing low spectator turnout seen in past parades by considering shorter parade lengths, college marching bands, and staging cannons at Sharp Field. Next, the parade working group will review route alternatives and coordinate planning with public safety officials.

positions.detail: Supports the expanded celebration and is actively exploring route options, staging locations, and entertainment to increase spectator turnout.

tricentennial-street-banners.name: Tricentennial commemorative street banners
tricentennial-street-banners.description: Permitting and installation of celebratory banners on utility poles across Southborough's historic villages.
tricentennial-street-banners.status: Town administration is coordinating with utility companies to secure attachment permits for commemorative street banners across Southborough's historic villages. The Tricentennial Committee has approved visual designs and recently reduced proposed banner locations from 67 toward a cap of 50 poles to avoid extra inspection fees. Permitting remains pending with National Grid and Verizon before installation can move forward.

positions.detail: Approved visual designs and is actively coordinating utility permits, targeting a cap of 50 poles to minimize utility inspection costs.

tricentennial-summer-nights.name: Summer Nights 2027 music festival
tricentennial-summer-nights.description: Expansion of the annual Summer Nights community event into a multi-act music festival for the 2027 Tricentennial.
tricentennial-summer-nights.status: Planning is underway to expand the annual Summer Nights event into a multi-stage music festival on August 21, 2027, at the Neary School grounds for the town's Tricentennial. The Tricentennial Committee is currently finalizing stage specifications, securing a headlining act, and pursuing grant funding for accessibility features such as shuttle services and a hospitality tent. Organizers will next coordinate site layout and logistics with the recreation, police, and fire departments.

positions.detail: Actively advancing plans for the expanded August 2027 festival, including stage specifications, performer agreements, and grant funding.

tricentennial-summer-nights.next: Submission of grant application for festival accessibility features on October 18, 2026

tricentennial-time-capsule.name: Tricentennial time capsule
tricentennial-time-capsule.description: Selection, preservation, and public placement of a commemorative time capsule for Southborough's 300th anniversary.
tricentennial-time-capsule.status: The Tricentennial Committee is moving forward with an above-ground time capsule display inside a public building to protect archival records and avoid underground enclosure costs. Committee members are currently coordinating offline on item collection protocols with assistance from Boy Scout Troop 1. A formal recommendation on placement is expected to go before the Select Board.

positions.detail: Supports an above-ground indoor display to protect photographs and written records while keeping preservation costs down.

trottier-finn-expansion-studies.name: Trottier and Finn expansion feasibility studies
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting articles to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools to reconfigure grade levels and take Neary School offline.
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.status: The School Committee, Select Board, and Advisory Committee all recommend defeating Articles 2 and 3 to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools at the March 2, 2026 Special Town Meeting, warning that additions would be required to prevent severe programming cuts.

trottier-school-roof-replacement.name: Trottier Middle School roof replacement
trottier-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed funding and MSBA grant reimbursement to replace the roof at Trottier Middle School.
trottier-school-roof-replacement.status: The proposed Trottier Middle School roof replacement is currently part of the district's reshuffled FY27 capital plan, with a gross estimate of nearly $8.9 million and an anticipated 41% MSBA reimbursement. The project will require Town Meeting to vote on the full gross authorization amount rather than the net cost after reimbursement. The School Committee supports the project and has focused on educating voters about the project's funding structure.

positions.detail: Supports advancing the roof replacement and voted 4-0 on March 24, 2026, to approve an informational flyer explaining the gross authorization and net cost to taxpayers.

two-family-zoning-amendment.name: Two-family dwelling zoning amendment
two-family-zoning-amendment.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment for Town Meeting to eliminate the requirement that a single-family dwelling exist for two years before converting to a two-family home.
two-family-zoning-amendment.status: The proposed zoning amendment to eliminate the two-year waiting period for converting single-family homes into two-family dwellings is headed to Special Town Meeting as Article 2. The Zoning Board of Appeals and Select Board support the article, but the Advisory Committee voted against recommending it due to concerns over speculative house-flipping, septic impacts, and increased density. The Planning Board has not yet taken a formal stance as members weigh whether the text creates unintended loopholes in commercial districts. The Planning Board will conclude its public hearing on the morning of October 17, 2026, ahead of Special Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Sponsored the amendment and voted unanimously on Oct 7 to advance Article 2 to Town Meeting as drafted.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 24 to support the revised article on the Special Town Meeting warrant.
Voted 3-4 on Sep 16 against recommending approval, citing worries about property flipping, smaller lot sizes in Residential B zones, and septic capacity.
Has not voted on a recommendation while reviewing how lot size baselines apply across residential and commercial zoning districts.
A former Planning Board chair warned that repeating district lot-size requirements creates ambiguity that could allow two-family homes on undersized commercial lots.

two-family-zoning-amendment.next: Planning Board public hearing continuation on October 17, 2026 at 9:05 AM

well-and-septic-regulations.name: Well and septic regulation amendments
well-and-septic-regulations.description: Board of Health regulations governing private well testing, swimming pool setbacks, and subsurface sewage disposal systems.
well-and-septic-regulations.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved the amendments to Southborough's private well and subsurface sewage disposal regulations following a public hearing in July 2026. The updated rules separate roles for septic design and installation, mandate repair access, establish a 25-foot setback between new wells and swimming pools, and require well testing prior to home sales with a mutual opt-out provision. No further board action or review is pending.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on July 7, 2026, to adopt the updated well and septic regulations as presented.
